key_insight: A physics-guided ML pipeline can separate the effects of crowding, composition, and bond flexibility on anomalous transport in crowded colloidal media.
engineering_relevance: The framework gives materials engineers a way to identify which microstructural knobs most strongly control particle mobility and relaxation in heterogeneous networks.
method: Brownian Cluster Dynamics simulations of binary colloidal systems
Surrogate machine-learning models trained on structural and transport descriptors
SHAP-based interpretation to attribute transport changes to specific physical parameters
evidence_signal: The authors evaluate the approach with mean-squared displacement, intermediate scattering functions, displacement distributions, and structural descriptors, showing that network formation increases transient caging while bond flexibility speeds post-network relaxation.
watch_item: The interpretation is based on simulated binary colloidal systems, so transfer to more complex or experimental crowded media will need validation.
paper_title: Physics-Guided Interpretable Machine Learning Framework for Anomalous Transport in Crowded Media with Tunable Flexibility
